techniques.name: Boot or Logon Initialization Scripts
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use scripts automatically executed at boot or logon initialization to establish persistence.

techniques.name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
techniques.summary: Adversaries may exploit software vulnerabilities in order to elevate privileges.

techniques.name: Obfuscated Files or Information
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to make a payload or file difficult to discover or analyze by encrypting, encoding, or otherwise obfuscating its contents on the device or in transit.

techniques.name: Steganography
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use steganography techniques in order to prevent the detection of hidden information.

techniques.name: Software Packing
techniques.summary: Adversaries may perform software packing to conceal their code.

techniques.name: Download New Code at Runtime
techniques.summary: Adversaries may download and execute dynamic code not included in the original application package after installation.

techniques.name: Stored Application Data
techniques.summary: Adversaries may try to access and collect application data resident on the device.

techniques.name: Clipboard Data
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse clipboard manager APIs to obtain sensitive information copied to the device clipboard.

techniques.name: Input Capture
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use methods of capturing user input to obtain credentials or collect information.

techniques.name: Keylogging
techniques.summary: Adversaries may log user keystrokes to intercept credentials or other information from the user as the user types them.

techniques.name: GUI Input Capture
techniques.summary: Adversaries may mimic common operating system GUI components to prompt users for sensitive information with a seemingly legitimate prompt.

techniques.name: Software Discovery
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of applications that are installed on a device.

techniques.name: Security Software Discovery
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of security applications and configurations that are installed on a device.

techniques.name: File and Directory Discovery
techniques.summary: Adversaries may enumerate files and directories or search in specific device locations for desired information within a filesystem.

techniques.name: System Network Connections Discovery
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of network connections to or from the compromised device they are currently accessing or from remote systems by querying for information over the network.

techniques.name: System Network Configuration Discovery
techniques.summary: Adversaries may look for details about the network configuration and settings, such as IP and/or MAC addresses, of devices they access or through information discovery of remote systems.

techniques.name: Internet Connection Discovery
techniques.summary: Adversaries may check for Internet connectivity on compromised systems.

techniques.name: Wi-Fi Discovery
techniques.summary: Adversaries may search for information about Wi-Fi networks, such as network names and passwords, on compromised systems.

techniques.name: Network Service Scanning
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of services running on remote hosts, including those that may be vulnerable to remote software exploitation.

techniques.name: Process Discovery
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to get information about running processes on a device.

techniques.name: System Information Discovery
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to get detailed information about a device’s operating system and hardware, including versions, patches, and architecture.

techniques.name: Exploitation of Remote Services
techniques.summary: Adversaries may exploit remote services of enterprise servers, workstations, or other resources to gain unauthorized access to internal systems once inside of a network.

techniques.name: Audio Capture
techniques.summary: Adversaries may capture audio to collect information by leveraging standard operating system APIs of a mobile device.

techniques.name: Location Tracking
techniques.summary: Adversaries may track a device’s physical location through use of standard operating system APIs via malicious or exploited applications on the compromised device.

techniques.name: Remote Device Management Services
techniques.summary: An adversary may use access to cloud services (e.g.

techniques.name: Impersonate SS7 Nodes
techniques.summary: Adversaries may exploit the lack of authentication in signaling system network nodes to track the location of mobile devices by impersonating a node.

techniques.name: Application Layer Protocol
techniques.summary: Adversaries may communicate using application layer protocols to avoid detection/network filtering by blending in with existing traffic.

techniques.name: Web Protocols
techniques.summary: Adversaries may communicate using application layer protocols associated with web protocols traffic to avoid detection/network filtering by blending in with existing traffic.

techniques.name: SIM Card Swap
techniques.summary: Adversaries may gain access to mobile devices through transfers or swaps from victims’ phone numbers to adversary-controlled SIM cards and mobile devices.

techniques.name: Abuse Accessibility Features
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse accessibility features in Android devices to steal sensitive data and to spread malware to other devices.

techniques.name: Drive-By Compromise
techniques.summary: Adversaries may gain access to a system through a user visiting a website over the normal course of browsing.

techniques.name: Replication Through Removable Media
techniques.summary: Adversaries may move onto devices by exploiting or copying malware to devices connected via USB.

techniques.name: Lockscreen Bypass
techniques.summary: An adversary with physical access to a mobile device may seek to bypass the device’s lockscreen.

techniques.name: Network Denial of Service
techniques.summary: Adversaries may perform Network Denial of Service (DoS) attacks to degrade or block the availability of targeted resources to users.

techniques.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
techniques.summary: An adversary may encrypt files stored on a mobile device to prevent the user from accessing them.

techniques.name: Supply Chain Compromise
techniques.summary: Adversaries may manipulate products or product delivery mechanisms prior to receipt by a final consumer for the purpose of data or system compromise.

techniques.name: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
techniques.summary: Adversaries may manipulate products or product delivery mechanisms prior to receipt by a final consumer for the purpose of data or system compromise.

techniques.name: Compromise Hardware Supply Chain
techniques.summary: Adversaries may manipulate hardware components in products prior to receipt by a final consumer for the purpose of data or system compromise.

techniques.name: Compromise Software Supply Chain
techniques.summary: Adversaries may manipulate application software prior to receipt by a final consumer for the purpose of data or system compromise.

techniques.name: Web Service
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use an existing, legitimate external Web service as a means for relaying data to/from a compromised system.

techniques.name: Dead Drop Resolver
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use an existing, legitimate external Web service to host information that points to additional command and control (C2) infrastructure.

techniques.name: Bidirectional Communication
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use an existing, legitimate external Web service channel as a means for sending commands to and receiving output from a compromised system.

techniques.name: One-Way Communication
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use an existing, legitimate external Web service channel as a means for sending commands to a compromised system without receiving return output.

techniques.name: Non-Standard Port
techniques.summary: Adversaries may generate network traffic using a protocol and port pairing that are typically not associated.

techniques.name: Video Capture
techniques.summary: An adversary can leverage a device’s cameras to gather information by capturing video recordings.

techniques.name: Screen Capture
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use screen capture to collect additional information about a target device, such as applications running in the foreground, user data, credentials, or other sensitive information.

techniques.name: Input Injection
techniques.summary: A malicious application can inject input to the user interface to mimic user interaction through the abuse of Android's accessibility APIs.

techniques.name: Access Notifications
techniques.summary: Adversaries may collect data within notifications sent by the operating system or other applications.

techniques.name: Encrypted Channel
techniques.summary: Adversaries may explicitly employ a known encryption algorithm to conceal command and control traffic rather than relying on any inherent protections provided by a communication protocol.

techniques.name: Symmetric Cryptography
techniques.summary: Adversaries may employ a known symmetric encryption algorithm to conceal command and control traffic, rather than relying on any inherent protections provided by a communication protocol.

techniques.name: Asymmetric Cryptography
techniques.summary: Adversaries may employ a known asymmetric encryption algorithm to conceal command and control traffic, rather than relying on any inherent protections provided by a communication protocol.

techniques.name: SSL Pinning
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use [SSL Pinning](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1521/003) to protect the C2 traffic from being intercepted and analyzed.

techniques.name: Archive Collected Data
techniques.summary: Adversaries may compress and/or encrypt data that is collected prior to exfiltration.

techniques.name: Data from Local System
techniques.summary: Adversaries may search local system sources, such as file systems or local databases, to find files of interest and sensitive data prior to exfiltration.

techniques.name: Foreground Persistence
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse Android's `startForeground()` API method to maintain continuous sensor access.

techniques.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
techniques.summary: Adversaries may transfer tools or other files from an external system onto a compromised device to facilitate follow-on actions.

techniques.name: Native API
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use Android’s Native Development Kit (NDK) to write native functions that can achieve execution of binaries or functions.

techniques.name: Compromise Application Executable
techniques.summary: Adversaries may modify applications installed on a device to establish persistent access to a victim.

techniques.name: SMS Control
techniques.summary: Adversaries may delete, alter, or send SMS messages without user authorization.

techniques.name: Scheduled Task/Job
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse task scheduling functionality to facilitate initial or recurring execution of malicious code.

techniques.name: Proxy Through Victim
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use a compromised device as a proxy server to the Internet.

techniques.name: Call Control
techniques.summary: Adversaries may make, forward, or block phone calls without user authorization.

techniques.name: Hooking
techniques.summary: Adversaries may utilize hooking to hide the presence of artifacts associated with their behaviors to evade detection.

techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse command and script interpreters to execute commands, scripts, or binaries.

techniques.name: Unix Shell
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse Unix shell commands and scripts for execution.

techniques.name: Event Triggered Execution
techniques.summary: Adversaries may establish persistence using system mechanisms that trigger execution based on specific events.

techniques.name: Broadcast Receivers
techniques.summary: Adversaries may establish persistence using system mechanisms that trigger execution based on specific events.

techniques.name: Hijack Execution Flow
techniques.summary: Adversaries may execute their own malicious payloads by hijacking the way operating systems run applications.

techniques.name: System Runtime API Hijacking
techniques.summary: Adversaries may execute their own malicious payloads by hijacking the way an operating system runs applications.

techniques.name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism
techniques.summary: Adversaries may circumvent mechanisms designed to control elevated privileges to gain higher-level permissions.

techniques.name: Device Administrator Permissions
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse Android’s device administration API to obtain a higher degree of control over the device.

techniques.name: Execution Guardrails
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use execution guardrails to constrain execution or actions based on adversary supplied and environment specific conditions that are expected to be present on the target.

techniques.name: Geofencing
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use a device’s geographical location to limit certain malicious behaviors.

techniques.name: Hide Artifacts
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to hide artifacts associated with their behaviors to evade detection.

techniques.name: Suppress Application Icon
techniques.summary: A malicious application could suppress its icon from being displayed to the user in the application launcher.

techniques.name: User Evasion
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to avoid detection by hiding malicious behavior from the user.

techniques.name: Conceal Multimedia Files
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to hide multimedia files from the user.

techniques.name: Impair Defenses
techniques.summary: Adversaries may maliciously modify components of a victim environment in order to hinder or disable defensive mechanisms.

techniques.name: Prevent Application Removal
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse the Android device administration API to prevent the user from uninstalling a target application.

techniques.name: Device Lockout
techniques.summary: An adversary may seek to inhibit user interaction by locking the legitimate user out of the device.

techniques.name: Disable or Modify Tools
techniques.summary: Adversaries may disable security tools to avoid potential detection of their tools and activities.

techniques.name: Indicator Removal on Host
techniques.summary: Adversaries may delete, alter, or hide generated artifacts on a device, including files, jailbreak status, or the malicious application itself.

techniques.name: Uninstall Malicious Application
techniques.summary: Adversaries may include functionality in malware that uninstalls the malicious application from the device.

techniques.name: File Deletion
techniques.summary: Adversaries may wipe a device or delete individual files in order to manipulate external outcomes or hide activity.

techniques.name: Disguise Root/Jailbreak Indicators
techniques.summary: An adversary could use knowledge of the techniques used by security software to evade detection.

techniques.name: Process Injection
techniques.summary: Adversaries may inject code into processes in order to evade process-based defenses or even elevate privileges.

techniques.name: Ptrace System Calls
techniques.summary: Adversaries may inject malicious code into processes via ptrace (process trace) system calls in order to evade process-based defenses as well as possibly elevate privileges.

techniques.name: Subvert Trust Controls
techniques.summary: Adversaries may undermine security controls that will either warn users of untrusted activity or prevent execution of untrusted applications.

techniques.name: Code Signing Policy Modification
techniques.summary: Adversaries may modify code signing policies to enable execution of applications signed with unofficial or unknown keys.

techniques.name: Virtualization/Sandbox Evasion
techniques.summary: Adversaries may employ various means to detect and avoid virtualization and analysis environments.

techniques.name: System Checks
techniques.summary: Adversaries may employ various system checks to detect and avoid virtualization and analysis environments.

techniques.name: Credentials from Password Store
techniques.summary: Adversaries may search common password storage locations to obtain user credentials.

techniques.name: Keychain
techniques.summary: Adversaries may collect keychain data from an iOS device to acquire credentials.

techniques.name: Steal Application Access Token
techniques.summary: Adversaries can steal user application access tokens as a means of acquiring credentials to access remote systems and resources.

techniques.name: URI Hijacking
techniques.summary: Adversaries may register Uniform Resource Identifiers (URIs) to intercept sensitive data.

techniques.name: Protected User Data
techniques.summary: Adversaries may utilize standard operating system APIs to collect data from permission-backed data stores on a device, such as the calendar or contact list.

techniques.name: Calendar Entries
techniques.summary: Adversaries may utilize standard operating system APIs to gather calendar entry data.

techniques.name: Call Log
techniques.summary: Adversaries may utilize standard operating system APIs to gather call log data.

techniques.name: Contact List
techniques.summary: Adversaries may utilize standard operating system APIs to gather contact list data.

techniques.name: SMS Messages
techniques.summary: Adversaries may utilize standard operating system APIs to gather SMS messages.

techniques.name: Accounts
techniques.summary: Adversaries may utilize standard operating system APIs to gather account data.

techniques.name: Dynamic Resolution
techniques.summary: Adversaries may dynamically establish connections to command and control infrastructure to evade common detections and remediations.

techniques.name: Domain Generation Algorithms
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use [Domain Generation Algorithms](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1637/001) (DGAs) to procedurally generate domain names for uses such as command and control communication or malicious application distribution.

techniques.name: Adversary-in-the-Middle
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to position themselves between two or more networked devices to support follow-on behaviors such as [Transmitted Data Manipulation](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1565/002) or [Endpoint Denial of Service](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1642).

techniques.name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
techniques.summary: Adversaries may steal data by exfiltrating it over a different protocol than that of the existing command and control channel.

techniques.name: Exfiltration Over Unencrypted Non-C2 Protocol
techniques.summary: Adversaries may steal data by exfiltrating it over an un-encrypted network protocol other than that of the existing command and control channel.

techniques.name: Account Access Removal
techniques.summary: Adversaries may interrupt availability of system and network resources by inhibiting access to accounts utilized by legitimate users.

techniques.name: Data Manipulation
techniques.summary: Adversaries may insert, delete, or alter data in order to manipulate external outcomes or hide activity.

techniques.name: Transmitted Data Manipulation
techniques.summary: Adversaries may alter data en route to storage or other systems in order to manipulate external outcomes or hide activity.

techniques.name: Endpoint Denial of Service
techniques.summary: Adversaries may perform Endpoint Denial of Service (DoS) attacks to degrade or block the availability of services to users.

techniques.name: Generate Traffic from Victim
techniques.summary: Adversaries may generate outbound traffic from devices.

techniques.name: Out of Band Data
techniques.summary: Adversaries may communicate with compromised devices using out of band data streams.

techniques.name: Compromise Client Software Binary
techniques.summary: Adversaries may modify system software binaries to establish persistent access to devices.

techniques.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
techniques.summary: Adversaries may steal data by exfiltrating it over an existing command and control channel.

techniques.name: Masquerading
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to manipulate features of their artifacts to make them appear legitimate or benign to users and/or security tools.

techniques.name: Match Legitimate Name or Location
techniques.summary: Adversaries may match or approximate the name or location of legitimate files or resources when naming/placing them.

techniques.name: Exploitation for Client Execution
techniques.summary: Adversaries may exploit software vulnerabilities in client applications to execute code.

techniques.name: Phishing
techniques.summary: Adversaries may send malicious content to users in order to gain access to their mobile devices.

techniques.name: Application Versioning
techniques.summary: An adversary may push an update to a previously benign application to add malicious code.

techniques.name: Data Destruction
techniques.summary: Adversaries may destroy data and files on specific devices or in large numbers to interrupt availability to systems, services, and network resources.

techniques.name: Remote Access Software
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use legitimate remote access software, such as `VNC`, `TeamViewer`, `AirDroid`, `AirMirror`, etc., to establish an interactive command and control channel to target mobile devices.

techniques.name: Exploitation for Initial Access
techniques.summary: Adversaries may exploit software vulnerabilities to gain initial access to a mobile device.

techniques.name: Virtualization Solution
techniques.summary: Adversaries may carry out malicious operations using virtualization solutions to escape from Android sandboxes and to avoid detection.

techniques.name: Linked Devices
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse the “linked devices” feature on messaging applications, such as Signal and WhatsApp, to register the user’s account to an adversary-controlled device.
